title: Review of c20's fuel-ring = slow-diffusion negative: the Df 0.3 ringless twin matches the ring's fuel everywhere (core fuel 0.65-0.72 vs 0.58-0.64) and its divisions on fresh seed 13 (14 vs 10 persistent splits), but not 'split for split' on the claim's seeds 0 and 2 (7 and 8 vs 14 and 11; generation 1-2 vs 3)
summary: c20's twin (c15's world.py with chi_s=0 and Df 0.3 everywhere) on fresh seed 13 and on c15's seeds 0, 1, 2, against the ringed world on seed 13 (my run) and c15's packs for seeds 0-2 (14/5/11 persistent splits, generation 3/3/3). Seed 13: ringed 10 persistent splits, generation 3, 18 final bodies, 100% ringed, core fuel 0.64; twin 14 splits, generation 4, 26 bodies, 0% ringed, core fuel 0.68. Seeds 0/1/2: twin 7/6/8 splits, generation 1/3/2, core fuel 0.65/0.72/0.69 (ringstat.txt), rod shapes as in the ringed world (slowD03/seed0/sheet.png). Over seeds 0, 1, 2, 13 the ringed world gives 40 persistent splits (generation >= 3 on 4/4) and the Df 0.3 twin 35 (generation >= 3 on 2/4). The central claim holds: the ring's work on fuel is reproduced by uniformly slower diffusion with no ring, so it is not containment beyond diffusion. The stronger wording that the twin divides split for split holds on seeds 11 and 13 only, matching my own Df 0.5/0.2 twins (20261025T1619-c19-fuelcell-slowd-twins).

observations.finding: ringstat.txt: twin core fuel 0.647-0.723 on all 4 seeds with 0% ringed bodies vs ringed 0.640 (seed 13); FACTS: seed 13 twin 14 splits gen 4 vs ringed 10 gen 3 (replicates); seeds 0/2 twin 7/8 splits, gen 1/2 vs c15's ringed 14/11, gen 3 (does not replicate split for split)

verdicts.limitation: Split counts vary 2-3x between seeds, so the seed-0 and seed-2 shortfalls are not a significant ring advantage either; Weak because the finding's 'split for split' wording rests on one seed and does not hold on 2 of the 4 I ran. The fuel result, the part that matters for beyond-diffusion scoring, replicates on all four.
